findings.problem: The plan contradicts itself on address duplicates. It explicitly says the 73 existing auto-filed abstract-page books remain and a later arXiv capture of the same paper will create a second book, but its completion criterion and test case require every book already held by address to be rejected without a request. The existing address check distinguishes owner books from auto-filed crawl books, so this distinction materially determines whether the stated migration behavior works.
findings.suggestion: Specify that only an owner-held address (or another precisely defined class) blocks the capture, while an existing auto-filed abstract-page book does not; add tests for both cases, including an existing auto-filed `/abs/` book leading to the new preprint.

findings.problem: The promised address form includes every arXiv id, while `capture_arxiv.parse_id` supports legacy category IDs containing a slash (for example, `cs/0112017`). The proposed parser must therefore handle `/abs/cs/0112017` and `/pdf/cs/0112017.pdf`, but the test list covers only single-segment modern IDs. A path-segment implementation could pass all listed tests while rejecting valid legacy papers.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit legacy-ID cases for both abstract and PDF address forms, including a versioned legacy ID if supported by the address form.

summary: The plan has a material ambiguity about existing auto-filed abstract-page books versus address-duplicate rejection; clarify it before relying on the implementation steps.
